response.justification: The candidate is an experienced full-stack/web software engineer with strong general development skills, but the resume shows no evidence of SoC/IP modeling, hardware architecture, GPU/accelerator work, or deep-learning performance optimization — the core requirements of this Principal Performance Architect role. Aside from some low-latency systems work at Dunnhumby and a C/C++ stint at National Instruments, the profile is a fundamental domain mismatch for hardware-software co-design and AI accelerator performance work.
strengths: 18+ years of software engineering experience, meeting the years-of-experience bar
Some low-latency, high-throughput systems experience (DLang, async I/O, caching at Dunnhumby)
Strong engineering practices (TDD, CI/CD) and open-source contributions demonstrating craftsmanship
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, hardware architecture, or hardware-software co-design experience
No deep-learning workload, GPU, SIMD/MIMD, or AI accelerator background
Career trajectory is web/full-stack product engineering, far from principal-level performance architecture

key_factors.factor: No AI/deep-learning workload or GPU experience
